medicine.label: Doctor
words: weigh up the risks and benefits
act in the patient's best interests

design.label: Designer
words: with the end user in mind

evidenceAudit.title: Evidence Audit
evidenceAudit.intro: List 8 experiences. For each one, say your own role, when, the scale (a number) and how someone else could check it.

fields.label: Experience
fields.hint: What did you do? Start with a verb.

fields.label: Role
fields.hint: What was your own part? Not the team's.
fields.example: Weekend volunteer: feeding, walking, adoption-day helper

fields.label: Scale
fields.hint: A number: people, hours, times, money, size.
fields.example: 35 dogs prepared for adoption; about 300 hours

fields.label: Link or location
fields.hint: Where is the proof? Paste a link or say where it is.
fields.example: Drive folder 'Shelter' / certificate in my portfolio

evidenceTypes.label: Certificate
evidenceTypes.description: A certificate, award letter or official record with your name, the organiser and a date.
evidenceTypes.example: Thai Red Cross first-aid certificate, 16 hours, March 2026

evidenceTypes.label: Link
evidenceTypes.description: A public web page, video or post that shows the work and your part in it.
evidenceTypes.example: School Facebook post about the stall, with your name in the caption

evidenceTypes.label: Photo
evidenceTypes.description: A dated photo of you doing the activity or of the result.
evidenceTypes.example: Photo of you at the shelter with the volunteer badge, July 2025

evidenceTypes.label: Witness
evidenceTypes.description: A named adult who saw your work and will confirm it (teacher, supervisor, organiser).
evidenceTypes.example: Khun Somsri, shelter manager, phone and email on file

evidenceTypes.label: Product
evidenceTypes.description: Something you made that can be shown: a model, report, app, design, video or booklet.

evidenceTypes.label: None yet
evidenceTypes.description: No proof yet. The claim cannot be checked until you find or create evidence.

unverifiable.label: Unverifiable
unverifiable.rule: evidenceType is 'none', or evidenceType is 'link' and the link field is empty
unverifiable.message: Nobody can check this yet. Find a certificate, link, photo, witness or product, or leave this experience out.

noScale.label: No scale
noScale.message: Add a number: people, hours, weeks, times, baht, or size.

evidenceAudit.c1Extension: Add a 'so what' to each row and rank the 8 by relevance to your target programme.

lineUpgrader.title: Line Upgrader
lineUpgrader.intro: Rewrite each weak line: start with a verb from the bank, add a number or a duration, and end with a result.

check.verb: The first word must be a verb from the bank (past form).
check.number: The line must contain a number (digits), e.g. 3, 120, 2025, 6 weeks.
check.result: The line must contain a result clause.

feedback.verb: Start with a verb from the bank, e.g. Led, Designed, Tutored.
feedback.number: Add a number: how many, how long, how much.
feedback.result: Add a result with one of these: which · resulting in · so that · leading to · earning · helping · cutting · raising · saving · winning. Then say what changed, in at least 3 words (…, which raised 4,000 baht).
feedback.pass: All three slots found. Now ask: would an admissions reader believe it?

lineUpgrader.peerPrompt: Would an admissions reader believe it?

lines.weak: I was in the school business club.
lines.model: Organised 3 pop-up stalls for the school business club in 2025, which raised 18,400 baht for the library fund.

lines.weak: Helped my aunt's shop with online selling.
lines.model: Launched a LINE shop for my aunt's dessert business over 4 months, resulting in 120 new regular customers.
Pitched a recycled-uniform start-up to 5 judges at a 2026 youth business contest, earning second place among 42 teams.

lines.weak: Good at managing money for the class trip.
lines.model: Managed a 65,000-baht budget for a 3-day class trip for 38 students, which finished 4,200 baht under budget.

lines.weak: Did market research for a café.
lines.model: Surveyed 150 students on drink prices for a school café plan, which showed that 35-baht drinks sold best.
Volunteered 60 hours at a community hospital's outpatient desk in 2025, helping about 40 elderly patients a day find the right clinic.

lines.weak: Went to a medical camp and did a presentation.
lines.model: Presented a dengue fever case to 30 students at a 2-day medical camp, which won the camp's best group presentation.
Taught hand-washing in 6 lessons to 90 Grade 2 pupils, resulting in 81 of them passing the school nurse's hand-washing check.
Trained 25 classmates in CPR after a 16-hour Red Cross first-aid course, so that every class on our floor has 2 trained responders.
Surveyed 80 parents in my district over 3 weeks about antibiotic use, which showed that 1 in 4 had bought antibiotics for a cold.
Assisted 2 dentists at a 1-day rural dental camp in Kanchanaburi, helping register and screen 150 children for tooth decay.
Built 12 clay tooth models in 8 weeks for an art elective, which a local dentist now uses to explain fillings to patients.
Measured the sugar in 20 school-canteen drinks for a science project, leading to 2 drinks being removed from the menu.
Interviewed 4 dentists during a 5-day clinic placement, which showed me how public and private dental care differ.

lines.weak: Helped kids not be scared of the dentist.
lines.model: Designed a 10-page picture book about a first dental visit, which a children's clinic gave to 200 young patients in 2026.

lines.weak: Love animals and help at a shelter.
lines.model: Volunteered every Saturday for 18 months at a Bangkok dog shelter, helping prepare 35 dogs for adoption.
Produced a 2-minute rabies-awareness video in Thai and English, which reached 4,500 views on the school page in 1 week.
Tracked the weight and diet of 6 shelter cats for 10 weeks, resulting in 2 overweight cats reaching a healthy weight.
Interviewed 3 pig farmers in Ratchaburi about biosecurity on a 2-day field trip, which became our group's 15-page report.
Coordinated 12 volunteers at a district neutering day, so that 64 street cats were registered, treated and returned.
Programmed the sensors for our 4-person robotics team, which placed 3rd of 28 schools at a 2026 national contest.
Built 5 low-cost PM2.5 sensors and ran them around school for 6 weeks, which showed the gate was worst at 7 a.m.
Redesigned the drainage for my family's 2 shops after the 2025 floods, cutting water entry from 15 cm to under 1 cm.
Tested 4 bridge designs made of 200 ice-cream sticks each for a science fair, leading to a design that held 22 kg.
Calculated the savings of a rooftop solar plan for our school, which showed a 6-year payback the school board agreed to study.

lines.weak: Was treasurer of the student council.
lines.model: Tracked 140 income and spending items as student-council treasurer in 2025, which gave the council its first full annual account.
Tutored 8 Grade 10 students in mathematics twice a week for 1 term, resulting in all 8 passing the final exam.

lines.weak: Helped my family business with tax.
lines.model: Organised 12 months of receipts for my mother's online shop, so that her accountant filed the 2025 tax return 3 weeks early.
Analysed the 2025 financial statements of 3 Thai food companies in a 6-week online course, resulting in a 10-slide comparison for my class.
Calculated costs and prices for a 2-day charity bakery stall, which made a 46% profit margin and raised 9,800 baht.
Designed 15 posters for the 2026 school sports day, which the school reused on its social media page for 6,000 followers.
Illustrated a 24-page children's book on air pollution over 3 months, which the school library printed in 100 copies.
Redesigned the club sign-up page after testing it with 10 students, cutting sign-up time from 5 minutes to 1.
Prototyped 3 large-print menus for a café near school, so that 12 older customers could order without asking staff.

lines.weak: Took part in an art exhibition.
lines.model: Created 4 mixed-media pieces from recycled packaging for a 2025 district exhibition, earning 1 of 5 judges' awards.
Debated in 14 rounds for the school English debate team in 2025, which reached the semi-finals of a 32-team Bangkok tournament.
Translated 9 information boards from Thai into English for a local temple, so that foreign visitors could read its history.
Edited 6 issues of the school English magazine as section editor, which grew its readership from 300 to 750 students.
Interviewed 5 elderly residents about canal life for a 3-month oral-history project, which the district library now keeps.
Guided 20 English tours at a Bangkok museum during the 2026 school holiday, helping about 300 visitors understand the exhibits.

clicheHunter.title: Cliché Hunter
clicheHunter.intro: Tap the 10 clichés in this statement. Then rewrite 3 of them with concrete evidence.

banList.example: I have a passion for… / I am passionate about…
banList.replacement: Say what you did and how often: 'I have spent every Saturday since May 2025 at the clinic desk.'

banList.cliche: ever since I was a child
banList.example: Ever since I was a child, I have…
banList.replacement: Give the date and the event: 'In Grade 9, when my grandmother had a stroke…'

banList.example: From a young age, I…
banList.replacement: Name the age and what happened: 'At 13, I took apart our broken fan.'

banList.cliche: dream (my dream, dream job, dream university)
banList.example: It has always been my dream to…
banList.replacement: State the goal plainly: 'I want to train as a dentist and work in a provincial hospital.'

banList.cliche: I have always wanted / always been interested
banList.example: I have always been interested in…
banList.replacement: Show when the interest started and what you did about it: 'After the 2025 floods, I started measuring…'

banList.example: This programme will broaden my horizons.
banList.replacement: Name what you want to learn: 'learn how Australian hospitals train nurses to triage.'

banList.example: I want to make a difference.
banList.replacement: Say who will be better off and how: 'cut waiting times for elderly patients in my district.'

banList.cliche: make the world a better place
banList.example: …to make the world a better place.
banList.replacement: Pick one place and one problem: 'reduce plastic waste at Chatuchak market stalls.'

banList.example: I want to become a doctor because I want to help people.
banList.replacement: Say which people and what help: 'explain a diagnosis to patients who only speak Isan.'

banList.example: I am a hard-working student.
banList.replacement: Show the effort with a number: 'I rebuilt the prototype 14 times in 6 weeks.'

banList.example: I am a team player.
banList.replacement: Say what you did in the team: 'I wrote the code; my two partners built the frame.'

banList.example: I am a people person.
banList.replacement: Give one example of working with people: 'I calmed 30 anxious children before their check-ups.'

banList.example: I have strong leadership skills.
banList.replacement: Show a time you led: 'I led 6 volunteers and set the weekly rota.'

banList.example: I like to think outside the box.
banList.replacement: Describe the unusual idea itself: 'I used ice-cream sticks to test bridge shapes.'

banList.cliche: step out of my comfort zone
banList.example: This made me step out of my comfort zone.
banList.replacement: Say what was new and hard: 'I gave my first talk in English to 200 parents.'

banList.cliche: give back to society / the community
banList.example: I want to give back to society.
banList.replacement: Name who benefits and how: 'run free screening days at my old primary school.'

banList.example: This programme is a perfect fit for me.
banList.replacement: Name one feature of the programme and one thing you have done that matches it.

banList.example: …your prestigious, world-class university.
banList.replacement: Name the specific feature: 'the year of study at a partner university abroad.'

banList.example: It was a life-changing experience.
banList.replacement: Say what changed: 'Afterwards I switched my elective from art to biology.'

banList.example: The trip was eye-opening.
banList.replacement: Say what you saw that you had not known: 'I had never seen a dentist work without electricity.'

banList.example: I learned so much from this experience.
banList.replacement: Name one thing you learned: 'I learned to check a dog's gums for dehydration.'

banList.example: It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
banList.replacement: Say what the opportunity was: 'a 5-day placement at a district hospital.'

banList.example: I always go above and beyond.
banList.replacement: Say what you did beyond the task, with a number: 'I added 2 extra Saturday sessions.'

banList.example: My journey to medicine began…
banList.replacement: Use the event itself: 'My interest in medicine began in a hospital car park in 2024.'

banList.example: In today's fast-paced world, technology…
banList.replacement: Start with your own story, not the world: 'Last March, our school's air sensor read 95.'

banList.cliche: at the end of the day
banList.example: At the end of the day, what matters is…
banList.replacement: Delete it and state the point.

banList.example: …to reach my full potential.
banList.replacement: Name the skill you want to build: 'learn to read a balance sheet quickly.'

banList.example: I am a perfectionist.
banList.replacement: Describe one standard you set and how you checked it: 'I tested every sensor twice before each reading.'

banList.example: The Oxford dictionary defines leadership as…
banList.replacement: Start with your own moment, not a definition.

banList.example: …and the rest is history.
banList.replacement: End with what you will do next: 'Next, I want to study how vets in Taiwan control rabies.'

text.title: Practice statement: find the 10 clichés
text.body:
Ever since I was a child, I have wanted to become a doctor because I want to help people. In Grade 10, I volunteered at a community hospital for one month. It was a life-changing experience, and it was truly eye-opening. I saw nurses work twelve-hour shifts, and I learned so much about how a hospital runs.

I am a hard-working student and a team player. In our science club, I worked with four friends on a project about dengue mosquitoes. We collected water from 20 homes and found mosquito larvae in 7 of them. The project made me step out of my comfort zone, because I had to present our results to the village health volunteers.

I believe your programme is a perfect fit for me. Studying medicine in English will allow me to make a difference in rural Thailand. I will use every chance to learn.

feedback.banned: Your rewrite still contains a banned phrase: {cliche}
feedback.accepted: Accepted: no banned phrase and a concrete detail.
feedback.needsDetail: Add a concrete detail: a number, a date, a place or a name.

clicheHunter.rewriteRule: Accept a rewrite when it matches no banList pattern and contains a digit or a capitalised name/place.

peerReview.title: Peer review
peerReview.intro: Read your partner's draft once without writing. Then answer the 5 questions. Describe, don't fix.

questions.label: What I understood
questions.question: In one sentence: what does the writer want to study, and why?
questions.frame: What I understood was that you want to study … because …

questions.label: The strongest evidence
questions.question: Copy the sentence that proves the most. Why is it convincing?
questions.frame: The strongest evidence is … because it has a number / a result / a specific moment.

questions.label: Where a reader from abroad would stop
questions.question: Which word, abbreviation or Thai reference would an international reader not understand?
questions.frame: A reader from abroad would not know what … means.

questions.label: Why this programme
questions.question: Does the writer name a real feature of the programme and link it to something she has done?
questions.frame: I was not sure why … links to this programme.

questions.label: One change
questions.question: The one change that would help most. Describe it; do not rewrite it. Note any banned cliché you saw.
questions.frame: The one change I would suggest is … I noticed the cliché …

pitchClock.title: Pitch Clock
pitchClock.intro: Pitch for 60 seconds. Your partner rates you for 60 seconds. Then move.

criteria.label: Clear who and why
levels: Listener cannot say who you are or what you want to study
Who is clear; why is vague
Who and why are clear and linked to one moment

criteria.label: One proof with a number
levels: One proof with a number and a result the listener remembers

criteria.label: Delivery
levels: Read from notes; hard to follow
Steady pace, clear voice, eye contact most of the time
Natural pace, pauses at key points, eye contact throughout, within 60 s

frame.label: Who
frame.stem: I'm …, a Grade 12 student at …, and I'm applying for …

frame.label: Spark
frame.stem: What first made me want to … was … (one moment, with a date or place)

frame.label: Proof
frame.stem: Since then I have … (one activity line with a number and a result)

frame.label: Ask
frame.stem: What sets me apart is … I'd welcome the chance to … (what you want from this listener)

parts.text: I'm Praew, a Grade 12 student at Satriwithaya, and I'm applying for an international veterinary programme.

On my first Saturday at a Bangkok dog shelter, the manager gave me a bucket and forty names. By lunchtime I knew that caring for animals means noticing things: which dog has stopped eating, which one is limping.

Since then I've volunteered every Saturday for eighteen months and helped prepare thirty-five dogs for adoption. I also made a two-minute rabies video in Thai and English that reached four and a half thousand views in one week.

What sets me apart is that I connect animal health with public health, what vets call One Health. I'd welcome the chance to tell you how I'd use field study abroad to learn how other countries control rabies.
I'm Earn, and I'm applying for international engineering.
On a smoke day last January, I wanted to know where the dust at school was worst.
So I built five low-cost PM2.5 sensors. Six weeks of data showed the gate was worst at 7 a.m., and the school now asks drivers to switch off their engines.
I'd welcome the chance to learn how engineers abroad design for air and floods.

questionCards.text: You wrote that you … What exactly did you do yourself, and what did others do?
How do you know it worked? What changed because of it?
questionCards.listenFor: A number, a before/after, or an honest 'I don't know yet'.

questionCards.text: If we contacted the organiser of …, what would they say about your part?
questionCards.listenFor: Claim matches what a witness would confirm.

questionCards.text: What was the hardest moment in …, and what did you do next?
questionCards.listenFor: A specific problem and an action, not a feeling only.

questionCards.text: What would you do differently if you did … again?
Your statement says … first made you interested. What have you done since then to test that interest?
questionCards.listenFor: Steps after the spark (Station 1: Spark · Steps).

questionCards.text: Why this programme and not a similar one at another university?
questionCards.listenFor: One feature of this programme linked to her own experience.

questionCards.text: Which part of the programme are you most looking forward to, and why?
questionCards.listenFor: Names a real feature (from the official page) and a reason.

questionCards.text: You used the word … Can you explain it to me as if I were not from your field?
questionCards.listenFor: Short definition, everyday example, no new jargon.

questionCards.text: Is there anything in your statement you would describe differently today?
What is one weakness your statement does not mention, and what are you doing about it?
questionCards.listenFor: A real weakness plus an action.

questionCards.text: Where could this degree take you in ten years, in Thailand or abroad?
questionCards.listenFor: Realistic path linked to a Thai or international need.

L09.prompt: Which of these is EVIDENCE, not a claim?
options: A Thai Red Cross certificate for a 16-hour first-aid course, March 2026
L09.explain: A certificate names the organiser, the hours and the date, so someone else can check it.

L09.prompt: What is TCAS Verified meant to do?
options: Check activity records with the organisation that ran them
L09.explain: TCAS Verified certifies activities by checking them with the organiser (MHESI/CUPT, 2026).

L09.prompt: 'I helped at a dog shelter.' What is missing most?
options: Scale: how often, how many, how long
L09.explain: Without scale the reader cannot judge the size of the work.

L09.prompt: I ___ at the clinic every Saturday since May 2025. (volunteer · 2 words)
L09.explain: Present perfect for involvement that started in the past and continues now.

L09.prompt: Your teacher supervised the project and will confirm your role. Which evidence type is this?
L09.explain: A named adult who will confirm your role is a witness.

L09.prompt: Thai universities say the portfolio round judges…
options: the quality and accuracy of the content
L09.explain: TCASFolio exists so that design and cost stop mattering; content and accuracy do.

L10.prompt: Which line follows Verb + What + Scale/Result + So what?
options: I was responsible for the library.
Very active member of the science club.
Organised 3 book fairs for 400 pupils, which raised 12,000 baht for new books.
I really enjoyed helping at the library.
L10.explain: It starts with a verb, has numbers and ends with a result.

L10.prompt: Raised 18,400 baht at the stall, ___ in two new shelves for the library. (1 word)
Choose the best verb: '___ 8 Grade 10 students in mathematics twice a week for one term.'
L10.explain: Tutored = taught individually or in a small group.

L10.prompt: You still run the club. Which sentence is correct?
options: I have run the club since 2025.
I am running the club since 2025.
L10.explain: Present perfect + since for something that continues now.

L10.prompt: 'Designed 15 posters for sports day, which the school reused online for 6,000 followers.' Which part is the 'so what'?
options: which the school reused online for 6,000 followers
L10.explain: The so-what shows why the work mattered to someone else.

L10.prompt: Which opening is weakest for an activity line?
L10.explain: 'Was responsible for' hides what you actually did.

L11.prompt: What is the course order for a personal statement?
options: Why this programme → spark → close → evidence
Spark → evidence → why this programme → close
Evidence → close → spark → why this programme
Close → spark → evidence → why this programme
L11.explain: Spark → evidence → why this programme → close.

L11.prompt: Which sentence SHOWS rather than tells?
options: At 7 a.m. every Saturday for 18 months, I fed 12 dogs at a shelter.
L11.explain: Time, number and action let the reader decide for herself.

L11.prompt: Which phrase is on the course cliché ban list?
options: Ever since I was a child
L11.explain: Replace it with a date and an event.

L11.prompt: The course limit for the personal statement is ___ words. (number)
During the 25-minute timed Draft 1 in class, AI is…
options: allowed if you write an AI-use statement
L11.explain: Draft 1 is your own authenticated writing; AI comes later, as an editor only.

L11.prompt: Best replacement for 'This programme will broaden my horizons.'
options: This programme will open my eyes.
This programme is a perfect fit.
I want to learn how hospitals abroad train staff to triage patients.
This programme will help me reach my full potential.
L11.explain: It names what you want to learn; the others are clichés.

options: one line per paragraph saying what that paragraph does
L12.explain: One line per paragraph shows whether the order works.

L12.prompt: In peer review, the reviewer should…
options: describe what she understood and where she stopped
L12.explain: Describe, don't fix: the writer makes the changes.

L12.prompt: Which AI use is allowed for the Module 2 assignment?
options: Ask AI to write your 'Why this programme?' paragraph
Ask AI to point out unclear sentences in your own paragraph, then decide yourself
Ask AI to make your statement sound native
Ask AI to invent an activity
L12.explain: AI may check work, never write it (syllabus).

L12.prompt: Reviewer language: 'What I ___ was that you want to study design because…' (1 word, starts with u)
L12.explain: 'What I understood was…' is the first reviewer frame.

L12.prompt: Your reverse outline shows paragraph 3 has no evidence. What should you do?
options: Add one specific example with a number and a result

L12.prompt: Why is your peer reviewer from another field?
options: To test clarity for a non-expert, international reader
L12.explain: Clarity for an international reader is a rubric line (1 point).

L13.prompt: What is the order of the pitch frame?

options: I'm Fah, and I'm applying for medicine.
I've always been interested in health.
Since May 2025 I've volunteered 60 hours at a community hospital desk.
I'd welcome the chance to talk more.
L13.explain: Proof = one activity with a number.

L13.prompt: Close: 'I'd welcome the ___ to tell you more about the project.' (1 word, starts with c)
About how many words fit a calm 60-second pitch?
L13.explain: A clear international pace is about 130–150 words per minute.

L13.prompt: For the 60-s video, where should you look?
options: At the screen showing your face
L13.explain: Looking at the lens reads as eye contact.

L13.prompt: Which is NOT a Pitch Clock rating criterion?
L13.explain: The course rewards being understood, not sounding native.
